heading: INT. PRAIRIE CURLING CLUB - SHEET THREE - EVENING

units.text: INT. PRAIRIE CURLING CLUB - SHEET THREE - EVENING
A long strip of pebbled ice under hard white light.
Brooms stacked against the boards like rifles.
The air smells of cold coffee and wet wool.
Red numbers on the scoreboard: 6-6, final end.
COACH BERNADETTE FONTAINE, sixties, in a quilted vest and a toque with a pom-pom, stands behind the hog line with a clipboard she does not look at.
SKIP YOSHI HARADA, forties, crouches in the house, holding his broom like a staff and watching the stone's path.
RUKMINI DEVADASAN, nineteen, the rookie, kneels in the hack with the last stone and breathes through her nose.
Ice is keen.
units.name: FONTAINE

units.text: Keen and straight. Give it a touch of burn.
units.name: HARADA

units.text: She knows.
units.name: FONTAINE

units.text: Rukmini does not answer.
She tightens her grip on the handle, adjusts her slider, and glances once at the brass rim of the house.
Her breath fogs.
Her hands do not shake.
Weight is ten.
units.name: HARADA

units.text: Weight is ten and not a hair more.
units.name: FONTAINE

units.text: Rukmini pushes off.
The stone slides, a granite hum on pebble.
Harada steps aside.
Fontaine takes one slow step toward the boards, then stops, because she has promised herself not to move.
The stone curls.
The sweepers, two grey figures in the distance, drop to their knees and scrub.
Hurry. Hurry hard.
units.name: HARADA

units.text: Fontaine closes her clipboard.
Rukmini rises out of her slide, silent, and watches the rock inch toward the button.
It stops.
Dead centre.
Nobody cheers.
Harada puts a hand on his hat.
Fontaine nods once, then looks at Rukmini, and holds up two fingers.
Two.
units.name: FONTAINE
